text:
Katie D.: Early UX pass on the API credentials panel — focusing on rotation vs disable, permission hints, empty-state guidance, and accessibility nits. Wanted to capture decisions before the design review.

Alex C.: Can you paste the mock or drop quick screenshots?

Katie D.: Summary of intent: 1) Surface a high-severity banner above the key list for full-scope keys, 2) Make Rotate an inline, visible action (not buried), 3) Rotation issues a new key immediately and marks the old key as "Pending revoke — expires in 24h" with a countdown.

Maria G.: For the countdown, we should rely on an exact expiry timestamp from the backend and render it in an aria-live region so screen readers announce changes.

Samir: +1. Also don’t rely on color alone for the banner — add an icon and a bold left border. The expiry announcement should trigger once when the key becomes inactive.

Katie D.: Proposed copy for the disable modal:

``"Disable API key?
This will immediately stop requests using this key. If you want a replacement, choose "Rotate" to issue a new key and keep the old one active for 24 hours.
```

Alex C.: Small wording nit: prefer "Disable API key" as the modal heading and reserve "Revoke" for audit terminology to avoid alarming language.

Jordan (PM): From product: Primary CTA should be "Disable key" (destructive). But make "Rotate key" a visible secondary action — rotation is a common path. Also capture permissions: only Owners and DevOps roles can rotate.

Maria G.: UX detail: show an inline permission hint below the Rotate button that reads "Requires Owner or DevOps role — Learn more". Make "Learn more" keyboard-focusable and link to docs.

Samir: Engineering fallback: if rotation fails server-side, keep the old key active and show a dismissible toast with error text and a contact-support link. Toast must be aria-live polite.

Katie D.: Empty-state suggestion: replace the single button with a 3-step mini guide: 1) Create a key, 2) Scope it to least privilege, 3) Add it to your app. Include a tiny curl snippet and an a11y note (buttons should have aria-describedby explaining consequences).

Alex C.: Copy tweak for the full-access banner — add two concise risk bullets under the banner: Exposure: anyone with the key can access data; Billing: unauthorized usage may incur charges. Also add a micro-link "Why restrict keys?" that opens a 1-2 sentence explainer modal.

Maria G.: Accessibility extra: keyboard focus should land on the modal primary action; make the warning indicator include text labels so color-blind users understand severity.

Samir: Technical ask: rotation endpoint should return { new_key, deprecation_window, expiry_timestamp }. UI should show the deprecation window until server confirms auto-revoke; consider a webhook to update the countdown instead of aggressive polling.

Katie D.: Can someone from infra confirm we get an exact expiry timestamp and whether a webhook is available? If not, we'll fall back to polling and show a small "synced at" timestamp.

Alex C.: I'll check infra and post back by EOD.

deploy-bot: Reminder: design review scheduled 2026-03-05 09:30 — calendar invite sent.

Katie D.: Thanks everyone — I'll update the Figma with: permission hint, the 3-step empty-state, revised banner bullets, and rotate/disable modal copy before the review. :thumbsup:
